context:
Phase-first, not query-first. Rule engine plugs in BEHIND existing
query-storage managers (catalog, dict-based, QUERY_VARIANTS) - no
storage-format migration. Typed CompatibilityContext + CompatibilityDecision
with enumerated support_level and failure_mode. Eight-action vocabulary
covering AST, regex-with-issue-link, session policy, variant selection,
DDL rewrite, benchmark gate, skip, and native passthrough. @compat_local
decorator + linter provides attribution so legitimate local rendering
(type mapping, storage layout) is not swept into the refactor. Migration
via feature-flagged dual-run harness with divergence telemetry; flip to
authoritative only after divergence reaches zero per slice.
description:
BenchBox's SQL compatibility decisions are currently scattered across five
structurally different sites: two bare-sqlglot translation cores with divergent
policy (benchbox/utils/dialect_utils.py:108 vs
benchbox/platforms/base/dialect_translation.py:33), hardcoded dialect tuples
inside primitives benchmarks (core/write_primitives/benchmark.py:171 and
core/transaction_primitives/benchmark.py:147), a _supports_primary_keys()
helper whose body contradicts the inline callers
(core/write_primitives/schema.py:352), unconditional PRIMARY KEY emission in
schema helpers (core/transaction_primitives/schema.py:130), regex-based
adapter transformers disabled in production due to SQL corruption
(platforms/clickhouse/query_transformer.py:47, routed around with a session
setting), benchmark get_queries() overrides patching in class-constant SQL
variants (core/h2odb/benchmark.py:106-141), plus scattered "dialect ==" checks
in schema generators (core/tsbs_devops/schema.py, core/nyctaxi/schema.py).

Result: the same capability (e.g., "does this platform enforce PK
uniqueness?") has three answers depending on which site asks, and some of
those answers are silent-corruption failure modes - StarRocks, for instance,
accepts PRIMARY KEY DDL but silently ignores PKs whose columns are not the
first N columns of the table.

This TODO builds a phase-aware compatibility subsystem (benchbox/sql_compat/)
that centralizes decision ownership across every compatibility decision point
surfaced by the inventory in w2. The final phase taxonomy is NOT frozen here:
w1 drafts the ADR with a provisional taxonomy, then w2 derives the final
taxonomy from the repo and the ADR is updated before engine work proceeds. Likely
candidates include benchmark_gate, query_source, query_compile,
query_adapter, schema_emit, ddl_optimize, execution_filter, and
dataframe_filter. Session policy is intentionally treated as an action, not a
phase, unless inventory proves a separate phase is required. Decisions are
made by a typed rule engine returning typed CompatibilityDecision objects
with explicit support_level, failure_mode, rule_id, and action payload.
Existing query-storage shapes (catalog-backed, dict-based managers,
QUERY_VARIANTS) remain in place - the engine plugs in behind each manager as
a resolver. Storage-format unification is an explicit non-goal of this
workstream and is deferred to a future ADR.

The migration lands in staged, reversible work units behind a
BENCHBOX_COMPAT_REGISTRY feature flag with a dual-run harness
(legacy + registry in parallel, divergences logged), cut over only after
divergence reaches zero. A
@compat_local decorator provides an attribution mechanism so a linter can
distinguish legitimate platform-specific rendering (type mapping, storage
layout) from unregistered compatibility policy. The linter lands warn-only
in the early inventory slice and is promoted to error during the
schema-generation cleanup slice before cutover.

See the ADR deliverable in w1 for the full design: phase taxonomy derivation
protocol, action enum, CompatibilityContext / CompatibilityDecision
dataclasses, rule_id format, baseline schema v1, dual-run harness spec,
DataFrame pipeline head design, and the storage-unification non-goal.

DDL FOLLOW-ON: Adapter-owned CREATE TABLE rewrites (ClickHouse, Databricks,
Databend, Firebolt, Redshift, Azure Synapse, Snowflake, Presto, Trino, Spark,
Lakesail, Velox) are tracked in `centralize-ddl-translation-phase`, which
runs in parallel with remaining items here. Those shadow harnesses register
REWRITE_DDL decisions while keeping the legacy _optimize_table_definition()
path authoritative until this item's w16 cutover. Fabric Warehouse is
excluded - its DDL hook is operational (schema-prefix injection via
self.schema), not a compat rewrite; see ADR section "DDL Centralization
Follow-On" for the full decision record.

anti_patterns.dont: claim slice w6 is 'zero behavior change'
anti_patterns.instead: gate with per-adapter snapshot diff sign-off
anti_patterns.why: dialect_utils.translate_sql_query applies identify-policy, SQLite fixups, and post-processors that the bare sqlglot.transpile in DialectTranslationMixin does not

anti_patterns.instead: derive the phase list from w2 inventory and freeze it in the ADR
anti_patterns.why: the reviewer proposed phases (dataframe_filter, session_policy as a phase, post_translate) mix phases with actions

anti_patterns.dont: leave vector_search/queries.py in files_affected without an owning work unit
anti_patterns.instead: onboard them explicitly in their own slice
anti_patterns.why: QUERY_VARIANTS plus platform-version gates are a distinct storage/decision shape

anti_patterns.dont: migrate without a reversible feature flag
anti_patterns.instead: ship behind BENCHBOX_COMPAT_REGISTRY with dual-run telemetry
anti_patterns.why: four slices touching ~15 sites across the codebase have no safe single-revert path

anti_patterns.dont: model capabilities as bare booleans (e.g., pk.uniqueness_enforced=True)
anti_patterns.why: StarRocks silently ignores PKs that violate the first-N-columns rule, which a boolean cannot express

anti_patterns.dont: revive the ClickHouse add_subquery_aliases regex rewrite
anti_patterns.instead: prefer AST; fall back to session policy if sqlglot cannot express the rewrite safely
anti_patterns.why: it corrupts Q23/Q87 parentheses and is disabled in production for that reason

anti_patterns.dont: ship 'no inline dialect == remains' as the acceptance criterion
anti_patterns.instead: gate on 'no unregistered-or-unexempted compatibility decision remains' instead
anti_patterns.why: legitimate type-mapping branches in nyctaxi/schema.py:253 and tsbs_devops/schema.py:174 are not compatibility policy

anti_patterns.instead: the benchmark_gate phase must back it via registry view
anti_patterns.why: it is enforced in CLI preflight at cli/commands/run.py:804

anti_patterns.dont: trust the reviewer's tpcdi/benchmark.py:374 citation without verifying
anti_patterns.instead: find the real site in slice w11 before registering the rule
anti_patterns.why: that line is a get_queries accessor, not a post-translation override

anti_patterns.dont: unify query-storage formats in this workstream
anti_patterns.instead: the engine must sit BEHIND the existing managers
anti_patterns.why: it conflates decision centralization with data-model churn and the dict-based managers have no blocking semantics today

preserves.behavior: CLI preflight in cli/commands/run.py:804 continues to fail-fast on unsupported (platform, benchmark) pairs
ClickHouse Q23/Q87 continue to run successfully (do not revive the corrupting regex)
DataFrame-mode skip decisions remain distinct from SQL-mode skip decisions (two pipeline heads share the registry, not the actions)
H2O Q9 ClickHouse and StarRocks variants continue to produce identical results to the current class-constant SQL
SQL/DataFrame engines that do not go through sqlglot (Polars, Pandas) retain their existing code paths
StarRocks first-N-columns PK rule is expressed structurally and prevents silent data divergence
Vector Search QUERY_VARIANTS and version-gated behavior continue to work without forcing sqlglot into the path
